item.title: Could an American win men's singles at this year's U.S. Open?
item.description: The Athletic's Lukas Weese joins CBS News to discuss who has the best chances with the U.S. Open tennis tournament underway in New York City.

item.title: 2 dead, about 15 missing after Grand Canyon hit by flash floods
item.description: Violent flash floods hit the Grand Canyon's Bright Angel Canyon and Phantom Ranch area, the National Park Service said, leaving more than a dozen people missing.

item.title: What to know after John Galliano's Met Gala exhibit canceled
item.description: John Galliano's exhibit for the 2027 Met Gala has been canceled after weeks of backlash over his past antisemitic and racist comments. CBS News fashion contributor Lauren Sherman reports.

item.title: Jury finds Duane Davis guilty in 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur
item.description: Duane "Keffe D" Davis, 63, was charged with murder with a deadly weapon with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal gang in Shakur's death.

item.title: Jury finds Duane "Keffe D" Davis guilty in 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur
item.description: A Las Vegas jury on Monday found Duane "Keffe D" Davis guilty in the 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur. CBS News legal reporter Katrina Kaufman has more.

item.title: One victim, suspect dead after Times Square stabbing
item.description: One of the two people stabbed in Times Square on Monday has died, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani says. The suspect is also dead after being shot by police.

item.title: Tropical Storm Edouard threatens Louisiana, Texas coasts
item.description: The National Hurricane Center issued a tropical storm warning for parts of the Gulf Coast of Texas and Louisiana ahead of Tropical Storm Edouard.

item.title: Camp Goldie features 13 golden retrievers: "Unless you're allergic to fur, what's not to like?"
item.description: Camp Goldie in New Jersey invites humans to "play dates" with its dozen or so golden retrievers. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Closing arguments presented in Tupac Shakur murder trial
item.description: The jury heard closing arguments Monday in the trial of Duane "Keffe D" Davis, the man accused of orchestrating the shooting that killed rapper Tupac Shakur. Celebrity attorney Chris Melcher joins to discuss the case.

item.title: 3 friends went hiking in the Grand Canyon. 1 died, 2 are still missing.
item.description: At least two people were killed and about 15 remain missing or unaccounted for after flash floods swept through parts of Grand Canyon National Park over the weekend.

item.title: Parents, coaches fighting at youth games leads to cancellations and bans
item.description: Two youth football coaches near Pittsburgh had a fight on the field over the weekend, earning suspensions from the league and adding to a growing list of adults behaving badly at their kids' sporting events. Mark Strassmann reports.

item.title: Growing backlash against data centers in American cities as poll finds over 70% oppose them
item.description: Tech companies pour trillions of dollars into new data centers, the backbone of the AI boom. But many communities across the U.S. are rejecting them. A recent Gallup poll found that more than 70% of Americans don't want data centers in their area. St. Louis is in the middle of the national fight, and Tony Dokoupil takes a visit.

item.title: Families of those missing after Nepal floods struggle to cling to hope
item.description: As the death toll from the Nepal floods surges over 900, Americans with loved ones among the 4,000 people missing are still hoping for miracles.

item.title: U.S. launches its first strike on Iran in over a month, regime retaliates
item.description: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submitted his resignation to President Trump on Monday. Over the weekend, the war with Iran entered its seventh month, with the first exchange of attacks in weeks. Weijia Jiang reports from the White House.

item.title: New info on Trump's expansion of "third country" deportations
item.description: Internal U.S. government documents obtained exclusively by CBS News show more than 100 deportees from Afghanistan, Cuba, Nicaragua and other countries have been sent to eight African nations. Some have criminal records, but many have no criminal history beyond immigration violations. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez has more.

item.title: Rare miracle in Nepal as 6-year-old pulled from jaws of death
item.description: Rescuers continued their search, rescue and recovery efforts in Nepal on Monday. Around 4,200 people are still missing, and Nepal's national disaster agency said at least 903 people are dead. Ramy Inocencio reports.

item.title: Tropical storm warnings in effect from Louisiana to Texas
item.description: Tropical storm warnings were in effect from Louisiana to Texas on Monday as thunderstorms built off of a tropical depression around 100 miles off the Gulf Coast. Jason Allen reports and Rob Marciano has the forecast.

item.title: At least 2 dead from Grand Canyon flooding, 15 still missing
item.description: More monsoon rains, which triggered deadly flash floods in the Grand Canyon, hampered rescue efforts on Monday. At least 2 were killed in the flooding and 15 people are still missing. Matt Gutman reports.

item.title: Severe weather hampers Grand Canyon rescue operations after flash flooding
item.description: A search-and-recovery mission is underway in the Grand Canyon after deadly flash flooding ripped through the national park over the weekend. CBS News chief correspondent Matt Gutman reports.

item.title: New York City police shoot woman accused of stabbing 2 people in Times Square
item.description: The New York City Police Department is investigating after officers shot a woman in Times Square, who they say stabbed two people. CBS News' Tom Hanson reports.

item.title: Supreme Court continues to allow construction of Trump's White House ballroom
item.description: The Supreme Court divided 5-4 in allowing construction of the new White House ballroom to continue.

item.title: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigning after friction with Hegseth
item.description: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is resigning, the White House confirmed.

item.title: What to know about new U.S. oil deal with Venezuela
item.description: President Trump is downplaying concerns about a new oil reserve agreement with Venezuela that experts say could take years to get up and running. CBS News' Lilia Luciano has more.

item.title: Trump says new strikes against Iran "limited," Bessent says Iranian economy months from collapse
item.description: President Trump said Monday that the latest U.S. strikes against Iran over the weekend were "limited" while Iranian economy continues to face the wrath of U.S. sanctions. CBS News' Natalie Brand reports.

item.title: 17-year-old girl indicted in San Diego mosque shooting over livestream
item.description: A 17-year-old North Carolina girl has been charged with murder by aiding and abetting in connection with the deadly rampage at the Islamic Center of San Diego in May.

item.title: E&Y to award $100 million in bonuses for workers who show people skills
item.description: Management consulting firm EY said it will reward employees who demonstrate human skills, such as business acumen and judgment.

item.title: 8/31: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: U.S. and Iran exchange strikes for the first time in weeks; at least two dead, several missing after Grand Canyon flash floods.

item.title: Will Trump's Venezuela oil deal ease U.S. gas prices?
item.description: The deal involves developing 17 strategic oil fields in Venezuela, an undertaking that experts said could take years.

item.title: John Galliano's Met Gala exhibit canceled amid backlash
item.description: The Met's decision to highlight the work by designer John Galliano sparked widespread controversy due to his history of antisemitic and racist comments.

item.title: Trump says U.S. now has control of over 60 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves
item.description: President Trump announced a deal to grant the U.S. control of more than 60 billion barrels of proven Venezuelan oil reserves.
